  "text": "The man at the repair shop placed the clock between them.

“Nothing wrong with the mechanism,” he said. “Just needed cleaning.”

Anna watched the second hand pass the twelve.

“It was stopping at twenty past.”

“Dust can do that.”

He turned it over and showed her the little door for the battery. Her mother had taped a coin inside, so there would always be something to undo the screw.

“I left that where it was,” he said.

Anna paid him and carried the clock home in a bag. At each crossing she held it against her coat to keep it from knocking her knee.

Her brother was in the hallway, sorting the post into piles on the floor.

“Does it work?”

“Yes.”

“How much?”

“Not much.”

He nodded and opened another envelope. Beside him were three catalogues addressed to their mother, all promising things for spring.

Anna took the clock into the kitchen. There was a pale square on the wall where it had hung, with a darker patch above the nail.

She stood on a chair and lifted it into place.

“Straight?” she called.

Her brother came to the doorway.

“A little left.”

She moved it.

“There.”

Neither of them spoke for a moment. The ticking was louder than she remembered.

“I could put it somewhere else,” she said.

He picked up the bag and folded it along its old creases.

“No. That’s where we look.”

Anna climbed down. Her brother moved the chair back to the table, then pulled it out again and sat.

She put the kettle on. Before filling it, she glanced up to check the time."
